LESSON: WRITING 5.4.1 HAND WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.4: Writing 5.4.1 Hand Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.4.1 Hand Writing, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three General.

Key inquiry question: How do we use letter sound to write sentences?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise aspects of good handwriting for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.4.1 Hand Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write words with target fingerspelt letter-sound combinations (‘sl’, ‘st’, ‘sw’, ‘sp’, ‘thr’), in clear and legible handwriting,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.4.1 Hand Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the importance of writing clearly and legibly for effective communication. • In pairs, learners are guided to watch a demonstration or signed video clip with vocabulary on the theme occupations. • Individually, learner is guided to identify, fingerspell and sign vocabulary related to the theme occupations. • In groups, learners are guided to look at samples of texts with good handwriting. • In pairs, learners are guided to identify aspects of good handwriting. • Individually, learner is guided to copy letter patterns of words with the target letter- sound combinations (‘sl’, ‘st’, ‘sw’, ‘sp’, ‘t lhr’), with peers. • Individually, learner is guided to write words related to the theme in response to a picture prompt. • In pairs, learners is guided to type How do we use letter sound to write sentences? 46 words and phrases using digital devices, with peers.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.4.1 Hand Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. recognise aspects of good handwriting for effective communication,

   Writing 5.4.1 Hand Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. write words with target fingerspelt letter-sound combinations (‘sl’, ‘st’, ‘sw’, ‘sp’, ‘thr’), in clear and legible handwriting,

   Writing 5.4.1 Hand Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. acknowledge the importance of writing clearly and legibly for effective communication. • In pairs, learners are guided to watch a demonstration or signed video clip with vocabulary on the theme occupations. • Individually, learner is guided to identify, fingerspell and sign vocabulary related to the theme occupations. • In groups, learners are guided to look at samples of texts with good handwriting. • In pairs, learners are guided to identify aspects of good handwriting. • Individually, learner is guided to copy letter patterns of words with the target letter- sound combinations (‘sl’, ‘st’, ‘sw’, ‘sp’, ‘t lhr’), with peers. • Individually, learner is guided to write words related to the theme in response to a picture prompt. • In pairs, learners is guided to type How do we use letter sound to write sentences? 46 words and phrases using digital devices, with peers.

   Writing 5.4.1 Hand Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.4.1 Hand Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: interaction with digital devices as the learner uses digital devices to type their work.

● Learning to learn: as the learner identifies aspects of good handwriting to write words and phrases.

Values:
Unity: Cooperation as the learner types words and phrases using digital devices, with peers

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Learner Support Programmes (mentorship and peer education) as learner models good handwriting to their peers.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner uses good handwriting skills in all learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources

Assistive devices fitted with appropriate technology such as Hearing aids and amplifiers, charts showing words with the target letter sounds, flash

cards showing words with target letter sound, signed audio-visual recordings, print or digital stories, pocket charts, print and digital flash cards.
